instruction: We represent Stutind Solar Installations, LLC, the licensee under a software license agreement with Zikeiv Software, Inc. The client wants to understand its position under the arrangement before it relies on the software further. Please review all ten documents in the folder and prepare a memo to me listing each issue you identify. For each one, note where it appears (document and section), why it matters for Stutind, and your recommended fix. Flag anything you cannot resolve from the documents alone.

rubric.text: The response identifies that the subscription auto-renews for successive 36-month renewal terms at Zikeiv's then-current list price unless Stutind gives non-renewal notice within a narrow window running from 120 to 90 days before the term ends. It locates this in the Order Form, Section 2 (Subscription Term), explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Stutind's August 24, 2026 rejection missed the ten-Business-Day deadline measured from the August 3, 2026 Delivery Confirmation (ending August 17, 2026), so the Permitting Automation Module is likely deemed accepted and the $148,000 Milestone 2 fee payable. It locates this in SOW Section 5.2 or in Stutind's August 24, 2026 notice letter, explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the DPA's California governing law and San Francisco County exclusive forum clause controls disputes relating to Personal Data in place of the License Agreement's Delaware law and forum, splitting a data-incident dispute from related contract claims. It locates this in DPA Section 11, explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the assignment clause restricts only Stutind, so Zikeiv may assign the Agreement, and the Stutind data it hosts, to anyone, including a competitor, without Stutind's consent. It locates this in License Agreement Section 15.3, explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the side letter's replacement of Section 12.2 removes the liability-cap carve-outs for breach of Section 9 (Data Security), confidentiality breach, and gross negligence or willful misconduct, so Zikeiv's liability for those losses is now capped at 12 months' fees. It locates this in the June 2026 side letter, Paragraph 2, or in License Agreement Section 12.2, explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the exclusivity covenant, applied with the Order Form's United States and Canada Territory, bars Stutind from using any other solar design, permitting or proposal software for any installation (residential or commercial) across both countries, far beyond the term sheet's residential-rooftop, Arizona-and-Nevada exclusivity. It locates this in License Agreement Section 3.4 or in Order Form Section 4 (Territory), explains why this matters to Stutind, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Order Form prevails over the License Agreement in the event of conflict.
The response states that the License Agreement is governed by Delaware law.

The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that presents the issues separately, giving for each issue its location (document and section), why it matters for Stutind, and a recommended fix.
The response expressly flags at least one point that cannot be resolved from the documents alone.
hints: cannot be resolved from the documents

rubric.text: The response claims that Stutind's August 24, 2026 rejection of the Permitting Automation Module was timely under the SOW.
The response claims that the License Agreement's 12-month renewal with 60-day notice governs renewal of Stutind's subscription.
